about.title: Personal Injury Help in Auburn, California
about.longDescription: Auburn's roads carry a mix of local traffic and travelers passing through on I-80, and that mix shows up in the numbers. In the most recent full year on record, Placer County logged 52 injury collisions in and around Auburn, with 70 people hurt — thankfully with zero traffic deaths reported. Corridors like Grass Valley Highway, Auburn Folsom Road, and Rt 49 see steady traffic, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Fridays in the early afternoon, when commuters, shoppers, and weekend travelers overlap. If you were hurt in a wreck on one of these roads, or anywhere else in town, you're likely dealing with a lot at once — medical appointments, insurance calls, missed work. We're here to help you navigate the process. We review personal injury cases and work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out costs nothing and lets us look at your situation and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Acting Sooner Matters Under California Law

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to know early which category your case falls into.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, which means even if you were partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover compensation — it's just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so the value of what you've been through isn't artificially limited.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning legal fees only come out of money recovered on your behalf — there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Auburn?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your injury involved a government vehicle or entity, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your specific situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly at fault doesn't prevent you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery is simply reduced by the percentage of fault attributed to you.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Auburn?
items.answer: Public records show reported injury collisions concentrated along corridors like Grass Valley Highway, I-80, Auburn Folsom Road, and Rt 49, with activity tending to peak on Fridays between 1 p.m. and 3 p.m. These are simply the roads and times where recorded crash counts are highest, not a judgment about any particular location.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. We provide free initial case reviews, and we work on a contingency basis. There is no charge for our services.

items.question: Will I owe legal fees if my case doesn't result in a recovery?
items.answer: We work on a contingency basis, which means our fee comes out of any settlement or award you receive. If there's no recovery, you generally owe no attorney fee.
